question: After the no-op pacing bug is fixed, should OpenClaw keep ambiguous outbound rows pending without spending retry budget when no reconcile-capable adapter exists, or keep current main's fail-closed behavior?
rationale: That choice affects existing queue upgrade behavior, operator visibility, and message-delivery recovery semantics, so code review can identify the safer mechanics but cannot fully choose the product policy.

options.title: Accept pending-with-backoff after repair
options.body: Keep this mitigation once unavailable-reconciler deferrals skip replay pacing and have regression coverage, preserving future recovery potential for ambiguous rows.

options.title: Keep fail-closed until ledger design
options.body: Close or supersede this mitigation in favor of the broader delivery ledger and adapter reconciliation design tracked elsewhere.

options.title: Land only behind an explicit operator mode
options.body: Preserve current default behavior and add an opt-in policy only if maintainers want a staged compatibility rollout.

recommendation.title: Accept pending-with-backoff after repair
recommendation.body: Keep this mitigation once unavailable-reconciler deferrals skip replay pacing and have regression coverage, preserving future recovery potential for ambiguous rows.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the outbound recovery ownership boundary is the split of delivery queue recovery and storage into the current files.
